title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask

yaml.title: Swot Analysis of Django vs Flask
yaml.author: Benjamin Panackal

markdown.markdown:
A sleep and study habits project needs a simple website to recruit student participants. 
They need a site with a short description of the
study, an eligibility screener of about eight questions, and a sign-up form that collects a 
name and email for people who qualify. Ideally, research assistants could also log in and see a list of sign-ups. 
Since site will hold contact information,security and privacy matter, and campus IT will want to know how the 
data is stored. The graduate student has never built a website, and the lab may re-use the website for future studies.
The website will not be maintained full time.
What would be a better choice to solve this problem: Django or Flask?

__Simple Conclusion:__ Django would be a better fit.

# Swot Analysis
## Django 
* Strengths
  * Built in security features protect your website from:
    * Cross-site scripting (XSS) protection
    * SQL injection protection
    * Clickjacking protection
    * Read [here](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.1/topics/security/) for more
  * Sanitizes user input by default (Cleans it to remove harmful elements)
* Weaknesses
  * Steep learning curve for a beginner, since it is a full-stack web framework vs. a micro one.
  * A bit heavier than what the project requires (it only needs a simple website without much functionality)
* Opportunities
* Threats

## Flask
* Strengths
  * Easy learning curve, since it is a micro-web framework 
  * Ideal for smaller scale projects like these
* Weaknesses
  * No built in security features, requires extra effort from the developer to protect against things that Django
  automatically protects against
  * Automatically trusts user input
* Opportunities
* Threats


# Recommendation
__Django__ is the better choice. It would pose a steeper learning curve and be a more comprehensive framwork 
then the project needs, but it is overall the safer option. Due to the graduate student's lack of experience with web
development, there could be potential security risks and slight oversights made due to inexperience. Django has built
in security features as opposed to Flask, which overall makes it the safer choice.


# Citations
* GeeksforGeeks (2025) Differences between Django vs flask, GeeksforGeeks. Available at: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/python/differences-between-django-vs-flask/ (Accessed: 28 October 2026). 
* Security in Django | Django documentation. (n.d.). Django Project. https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.1/topics/security/
* Corgea. (2026, August 28). Flask Security Best Practices 2026 | Corgea. Corgea. https://corgea.com/learn/flask-security-best-practices-2025
